reason: Reproduced end to end on a copy of the lab in collateral, never in the lab. Baseline: 461 assertions, 0 failing. The code reading is exact. interaction-check.mjs:960-964 walks .kpi and calls check(el.textContent) and check(el.querySelector('.sr')?.textContent); lately.html:745 renders each status card as a div.kpi with role=group and an aria-label and no .sr child, so the second call is passed undefined and returns on check's first line (if (!s) return). The third sweep reads 'main p, main span, .sr' - textContent only, never a name. Both regexes require the noun ('jobs' then has|is|was, and '1 job' then have|are|were|haven't|aren't), and the noun appears nowhere on screen: the face is a t-num span holding '3' and a separate t-small span holding 'hasn't moved in a fortnight', so no string this block can ever see contains a numeral joined to a verb by job/jobs. Line 1547 is the only other reader of a status card's name and it takes .length > 12. Three planted defects, each run alone against the full gate: (a) lately.html:726 'const phrase = word.one' - the row then speaks '2 jobs is past the day it was due, of 9 jobs open' and '3 jobs hasn't moved in a fortnight', a literal hit for the block's own first regex, and prints '3 hasn't moved in a fortnight' / '2 is past the day it was due' on screen - 461 assertions, 0 failing; (b) 'const phrase = word.many' - '1 job have nobody's name on them', a literal hit for the second regex, and the exact sentence the closed r1 finding count-of-one-takes-a-plural-verb was raised for - 461 assertions, 0 failing; (c) lately.html:729 denominator falsified to plural(D.open + 3, ...) - every card announced 'of 12 jobs open' beside a lead plate reading 9, the protected shared-denominator contract wrong in the only channel that carries it - 461 assertions, 0 failing. Substituting aria-label="aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa" on all four cards fails exactly one assertion, 'unavailability is carried in words, not only in ink', and only via its 'not available' test - 461 assertions, 1 failing. The title claim is therefore literally true. Two corrections that do not move the verdict: line 298 does read a status card's aria-label for content, but only for 'not available' on the single na card in ?state=partial - precisely the one assertion the aaaa plant tripped; and the row does not exist in every state - ?state=quiet renders a different movement two (lately.html:969) with no .kpi cards at all, so the states carrying the row are full, partial and first-run. This is a vacuous assertion sitting under a comment that promises 'on screen and in the accessibility tree, at 0, 1 and more', guarding the class the round notes rate above the defect that exposes it, and it leaves a confirmed r1 finding with no live guard. Severity 'defect' is right and not overstated: nothing on the shipped surface is wrong today - the names are correct - so this is neither misleading nor blocking, but the gate visibly claims a guarantee it cannot deliver, which is more than a refinement. The fix is gate-side only: no pixel moves, no constraint touched, the frozen structure is untouched.
sharpenedFix: Take the fix's first half unchanged - its numbers check out against the real source. lately.html:678 is plural = (n, one, many) => `${n} ${n === 1 ? one : many}` and :729 builds `${plural(n,'job','jobs')} ${phrase}, of ${plural(D.open,'job','jobs')} open`, so a prefix of `${shown} job ` / `${shown} jobs ` and a suffix of `of ${openCount === 1 ? '1 job' : openCount + ' jobs'} open` are exactly right, and window.LATELY_FIXTURE.bound.openCount is already read at line 204. The unavailable branch is right too - that name is 'Jobs past the day they were due: not available, because Timeline did not answer', no digit - but select it with card.querySelector('.na') rather than comparing .t-num against a literal em dash, a character the source only ever emits as —. Drop the fix's second half. Joining .t-num and .t-small with a space yields '3 hasn't moved in a fortnight' and '1 have nobody's name on them'; neither regex can match either, because both require the noun and the face never prints it - so as written that addition is a second assertion that cannot fail, the very thing being filed. Replace it with a synthesised face string - check(`${shown} ${shown === '1' ? 'job' : 'jobs'} ${card.querySelector('.t-small').textContent.trim()}`, 'card face') - which does fire on plant (a) via the overdue card and on plant (b) via the unowned card. Add one assertion the parse cannot dodge: the name must contain the visible .t-small text verbatim, so the tree and the face can never drift apart. Scope the new block to the three states that actually have the row - full, partial, first-run - and assert cards.length === 4 inside each, otherwise iterating quiet (no .kpi at all) makes the replacement vacuous in the same way it is filing against; and never widen it to loading, where lately.html:1026 renders a full-fidelity movementTwo, real names and all, inside aria-hidden. Then do what the finding says: write it first, plant each of the three defects in turn, watch the state assertions fail, restore.
breaks: Nothing on the surface - this touches only interaction-check.mjs. What it costs is coupling: a hard prefix/suffix parse pins the gate to the exact sentence at lately.html:729, so a future copy revision to the row's name, or a fixture whose openCount is 1, breaks the gate rather than the product; derive the assertion from plural()'s own rule (singular only at exactly 1) rather than from today's strings. The 'no digit in the unavailable name' clause breaks if the refusal copy ever names a numbered source. After it lands re-measure: the full gate green on the master at the new count (461 rising by roughly 9-12); each of the three plants failing at least one new assertion, individually, before restoring; the aaaa substitution now failing the new name assertions rather than only the 'not available' one; and the loading state still passing, to confirm the skeleton's aria-hidden cards were not pulled into the new sweep.
